status: Identity Access now has a bounded native assignment slice: a Company/branch/department assignment workspace read and a reviewed assignment withdrawal command. The owner slice includes portable domain/application ports, a PostgreSQL adapter over the existing assignments/IAM tables, an owner-local HTTP router, a strict Next transport, and configured IAM workspace/command cutover. The owner remains foundation: access reviews, role publication, grant/proposal, Directory administration, invite/emergency administration, identity conflicts and browser acceptance remain open; the native router is not mounted in shared composition.

scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified source slice is the current assignment workspace read used by the IAM overview/users/matrix/reviews pages and the existing `assignments/{id}/revoke` command used by the IAM assignment drawer and users table. Assignment grant/proposal, independent-review decisions, role publication, access-review campaigns, MFA, Directory connectors, identity conflicts, invitations and every other Identity Access workflow remain retained TypeScript.
scope.domain: Portable assignment policy: exact Company/selected Holding scope, `iam.read`/`iam.manage` requirements, selected-context expiry, branch/department exact-node withdrawal scope, bounded id/reason/version values, immutable role/source/status checks, self and same-Person refusal, last recovery administrator protection, last holding-owner protection, request-invalid and source-invalid failures.
scope.application: One assignment_workspace use case authorizes current read authority and validates bounded ordered Company-scoped rows and published role rows. One revoke_assignment use case authorizes current write authority, hashes the exact key/body/context, replays the committed receipt, locks the assignment, rechecks source/Company/scope/self/version/recovery/administrator guards, commits the revocation with receipt/audit/outbox, and reads back the revoked row plus cleared active work contexts. The application layer opens no transaction and reads no HTTP request.
scope.adapters: PostgreSQL SQL is Identity-owned (`assignments`, `iam_members`, `iam_identities`, `iam_connections`, `iam_mappings`, `iam_groups`, `iam_roles`, `iam_role_revisions`, `iam_audit`, `iam_revoked_sessions`, `active_work_contexts`) plus shared `command_receipts`, `audit_events` and `outbox_events`. No Organization, People, Finance, Directory or other owner row is mutated. The caller's serializable Holding transaction is mandatory; no transaction is started, committed or retried by the adapter.
scope.http: Owner-local GET `/api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/iam/assignments` and POST `/api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/iam/assignments/{assignment_id}/revoke`. The router requires exact registered Host/Holding targets, HTTPS origins, empty or strict JSON bodies, one valid Idempotency-Key, no query, bounded bodies, private/no-store, no-referrer and nosniff responses, and bounded BusinessError status mapping. The composition backend owns Account session resolution, current Company/branch/department scope, current IAM authority and the serializable owner unit.
scope.transport: `ERPX_NATIVE_IDENTITY_ACCESS_CONFIG` is strictly validated: literal loopback private base, reserved ports 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/5432/5433/5435/8080 and 3200-3299 excluded, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs, 250..30000 ms timeout, bounded Host/cookie/context headers, exact workspace/role/assignment/receipt/context shapes, row Company/scope coherence, unique ordered rows, and 2 MiB response bound. A configured failure never falls back to the retained reader or command.
scope.ssr: When the native configuration is present, `iamPresentationQueries.iamOverview` overlays the native assignment rows into the existing IAM overview for holding-scoped non-self pages; all other overview sections remain retained. The overview assignment rows therefore come from the native owner, while role grants, access reviews, Directory, MFA, invitations and sessions remain retained. A configured native read failure surfaces through the existing page/route error policy and never silently uses the retained assignment rows.
scope.commandCutover: In `packages/server-identity_access/src/adapters/iam-api.ts`, the existing `assignments/{id}/revoke` POST calls the native client when `ERPX_NATIVE_IDENTITY_ACCESS_CONFIG` is present and the actor is a Company/Holding actor. Without the configuration the retained TypeScript command remains the path; a configured malformed/failed native command is mapped to the existing ApiError surface and never falls back to the retained command.
scope.notClaimed: No browser journey, authenticated page render, shared composition mount, catalogue register update, role-grant proposal, access-review decision, MFA, Directory connector, identity-conflict, invitation, deployment, staging, private production or Cloudflare verification.
